queries.hook: A quiet house, a widower with time on his hands, and the wish to read the Gita as a life, not a forwarded line.
queries.diagnose: When life is lived only for what passes, the heart feels empty; meaning is missing when we forget what does not pass.

verse.speaker: Narrator
verse.setting: King Manu, who ruled well for a lifetime, sees that old age has come and something essential was missed.
verse.sanskrit: होइ न बिषय बिराग भवन बसत भा चौथपन॥ हृदयँ बहुत दुख लाग जनम गयउ हरिभगति बिनु ॥
verse.line: Old age arrived at home, the cravings stayed, and he grieved for the years spent elsewhere.
verse.translation: Old age came while he lived at home, yet the pull of pleasures had not faded. His heart grieved deeply that his life had gone by without devotion to Hari.
verse.why: It is not too late to turn towards what matters, but it takes courage to ask for it.

prasang.title: Manu and Shatarupa ask late in life
prasang.summary: King Manu and Queen Shatarupa realise in old age that a whole life has passed without what mattered most to them. They hand over the kingdom, go to the forest and practise austerity for years. When Vishnu offers a boon, Manu hesitates like a poor man before the wishing tree, then asks for a son like God himself.
prasang.story_hook: The king had ruled well for a lifetime, and one morning he realised he had missed the point.
prasang.lesson: It is not too late to turn towards what matters, but it takes courage to ask for it.

verse.meaning: King Manu has ruled for a lifetime and now old age is here. He looks back and sees that his heart was never turned toward what mattered. The life he lived was full, but the cravings stayed, and he grieves for the years spent elsewhere. This is what happens when the house is quiet and the mind turns back, not to blame, but to see clearly that it is not too late to ask for what was missed.
verse.for_you: The quiet house has brought the Sunday calls into focus, and now the rest of the week asks what you are turning toward. The Gita you want to read is not a forwarded line.

verse.speaker: Prajapati's teaching (narrator)
verse.setting: On the self in the heart that we visit nightly in deep sleep without knowing it.
verse.sanskrit: अनृतापिधानास्तद्यथापि हिरण्यनिधिं निहितमक्षेत्रज्ञा उपर्युपरि सञ्चरन्तो न विन्देयुरेवमेवेमाः सर्वाः प्रजा अहरहर्गच्छन्त्य एतं ब्रह्मलोकं न विन्दन्त्यनृतेन हि प्रत्यूढाः ॥
verse.line: Like people walking daily over buried gold, we pass our own treasure every day and never find it.
verse.translation: As people who do not know the spot walk again and again over a hidden treasure of gold buried in the ground and do not find it, so all these creatures go day after day into that world of Brahman and do not find it, for they are carried away by untruth.

matched.label: Nothing is wrong but nothing feels meaningful

verse.meaning: A teacher speaks to a student about the self that rests in the heart. The teacher says that people walk every day over buried gold without knowing it. They pass their own treasure and never find it. So all creatures go into that unseen world each night in deep sleep and do not find it. They are carried away by untruth.
verse.for_you: Your quiet house is not empty. It is the ground where you pass your own treasure every day without seeing it. The Gita you want to read is the map to what is already beneath your feet.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verse.sanskrit: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा । तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥
verse.line: Childhood, youth, old age: the body keeps changing. The wise aren't thrown by the next change.
verse.translation: Just as the embodied self passes through childhood, youth and old age in this body, so it passes on to another body. The steady person is not bewildered by this.
verse.why: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

prasang.title: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasang.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield. He says that just as the embodied self passes through childhood, youth and old age in this body, so it passes on to another body. The steady person is not bewildered by this. What truly is in you outlasts every loss and every passing pain.
verse.for_you: The body has changed, the house is quiet, the Sunday calls are the only rhythm left. But what reads the verse is not the body that changes. It is the part of you that was never born and will never die, and it is still here.

verse.speaker: Sumantra
verse.setting: Sumantra returns alone to the grieving king Dasharath and steadies him.
verse.sanskrit: जनम मरन सब दुख सुख भोगा। हानि लाभु प्रिय मिलन बियोगा॥ काल करम बस होहिं गोसाईं। बरबस राति दिवस की नाईं ॥ सुख हरषहिं जड़ दुख बिलखाहीं। दोउ सम धीर धरहिं मन माहीं॥ धीरज धरहु बिबेकु बिचारी। छाड़िअ सोच सकल हितकारी ॥
verse.line: Gain and loss, meeting and parting come like day and night. The steady hold both alike.
verse.translation: Birth and death, joy and sorrow, loss and gain, meeting and parting with those we love: these come under the sway of time and action, as surely as night and day. The foolish rejoice in good times and wail in bad; the steady hold both alike in the mind. Hold on to your courage, think with discernment, and let go of worry, you who care for everyone.
verse.for_you: The house is quiet, but the grief is not. The steady hold both alike. Let your reading be the courage that holds the loss, not the worry that fights it.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna begins his ladder of practices with the simplest instruction.
verse.sanskrit: मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय । निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः ॥
verse.line: Rest your mind in me, settle your thinking in me, and you will live in me.
verse.translation: Fix your mind on me alone, let your understanding settle in me; from then on you will dwell in me. Of this there is no doubt.

matched.label: I want to reconnect with my roots

verse.meaning: Krishna offers Arjuna a direct path to the divine, beginning with the simplest instruction. He asks Arjuna to fix his mind entirely on Krishna, to let his understanding settle only there. From this single act of steady focus, Krishna promises, Arjuna will dwell in him. The verse proposes that liberation is not found in complex rituals, but in the quiet, unwavering placement of your attention on what you hold most true.
verse.for_you: Today, as you sit in the quiet of your morning, place your mind on the verse itself.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna opens the teaching on knowing him fully.
verse.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः । असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु ॥
verse.line: Keep your mind attached to me, lean on me, keep practising. You will come to know me fully.
verse.translation: Hear, Partha, how with your mind attached to me, practising yoga and taking refuge in me, you will know me fully, without doubt.

matched.label: I want to reconnect with my roots

verse.meaning: Krishna is opening the teaching on knowing him fully. Arjuna is standing in a field of battle, but the real battle is in the mind. Krishna says that if you keep your mind attached to him, practice this steady focus, and take refuge in it, you will know him fully, without any doubt.
verse.for_you: Keep your mind on the text as you read. Let your morning reading be the practice that settles your thinking, so you can live inside the meaning of it each day.

story.title: Learned seers find no peace and go to Ganesha
story.story_hook: They knew every verse of every Veda, and still could not sleep.
story.summary: Seers who had received all the Vedas still found no peace, so they went to Ganesha's world and took refuge in him. Ganesha tells them that though he has no form, loving devotees see him in the form they long for, and that knowing his highest form brings lasting peace.
story.lesson: Learning alone may not settle the heart; turning to God can.

anchor.speaker: The seers
anchor.setting: Seers who had studied every Veda come to Ganesha's world because learning alone left them restless.
anchor.sanskrit: अतो नेवाभवच्छान्तिरस्माकं चेतसि प्रभो!। वयं शरणमापन्ना भवल्लोकमुपस्थिताः ॥
anchor.line: Lord, no peace came to our minds. So we have come to you for refuge.
anchor.translation: So no peace came into our minds, Lord. We have come to your world and taken refuge in you.
anchor.why: Learning alone may not settle the heart; turning to God can.

prasang.summary: Seers who had received all the Vedas still found no peace, so they went to Ganesha's world and took refuge in him. Ganesha tells them that though he has no form, loving devotees see him in the form they long for, and that knowing his highest form brings lasting peace.

story.teaser: The seers knew every verse of every Veda, and still couldn't sleep
story.for_you: You have read the Gita with care and know its words well. Yet the quiet house shows that knowledge alone does not settle the heart. Let the text be more than a study. Let it be the refuge you return to each morning until the stillness within becomes the lasting peace you seek.

script: The house is very quiet. You have retired, and your children call on Sundays. In between, you are searching for depth, wanting to read the Gita properly, not just forwarded lines. This is a real moment.

King Manu, who ruled well for a lifetime, sees that old age has come. He looks back and realises something essential was missed. And you hear the narrator speak to you: The quiet house has brought the Sunday calls into focus, and now the rest of the week asks what you are turning toward. Narrator said:
होइ न बिषय बिराग भवन बसत भा चौथपन. हृदयँ बहुत दुख लाग जनम गयउ हरिभगति बिनु.
In plain words: Old age arrived at home, the cravings stayed, and he grieved for the years spent elsewhere.

This is what happens when the mind turns back. It is not about blame. It is about seeing clearly. The cravings stayed, and he grieved. But it is not too late to ask for what matters. This takes courage. You do not need to fix the past. You only need to see what is in front of you now.
When you sit with your Gita today, let the craving for forwarded lines fall away. Ask what your part is in this quiet house, right now.
